capability_gaps.slash_commands: No plugin-shippable command mechanism found. All 9 plugins bundled with codex 0.156.0 (browser, chrome, codex-app-tools, computer-use, latex, messages, record-and-replay, unified-computer-use, visualize) were checked: 0 declare a commands manifest field and 0 ship a commands/ directory. Earlier: Schema-diff advance 2.0.15 -> 2.0.22 (2026-10-02, no live opencode binary in this environment; validated_against stays 2.0.14). Sources: npm @opencode/cli (2.0.16 09-24, 2.0.17/2.0.18 09-25, 2.0.19/2.0.20 09-29, 2.0.21 09-30, 2.0.22 10-02). The upstream release notes were NOT readable from this session: every anomalyco/opencode v2.0.x release page fails to render its body and the releases Atom feed answers 403, so this advance is recorded on evidence this repo can actually check rather than on prose. That evidence: packages/schema/src/config.ts, permission.ts, config/agent.ts and config/command.ts are byte-identical between the v2.0.14 and v2.0.22 tags, and the live https://opencode.ai/config.json still declares exactly the 15 PermissionConfig keys scripts/check-opencode-permission-keys.sh pins (bash, doom_loop, edit, external_directory, glob, grep, list, lsp, question, read, skill, task, todowrite, webfetch, websearch; --refresh re-read it today) with AgentConfig.tools still marked deprecated in favour of `permission`, which the generated agents already use. So the config/agent/command/permission surface this repo generates against did not move across the eight releases; runtime behaviour that may have changed cannot be reviewed without the notes or a binary and is flagged as such rather than claimed reviewed. Permission-key conformance (2026-09-23): the agent generator emitted `write` for every agent, which is NOT a key of PermissionConfig in https://opencode.ai/config.json (the 15 keys are bash, doom_loop, edit, external_directory, glob, grep, list, lsp, question, read, skill, task, todowrite, webfetch, websearch). Canonical Write now maps to `edit`, the key that actually governs file modification. No agent was over-permitted in practice - the read-only agents deny `edit` too - but the generator's allowlist guarantee was resting on a deny-list line that matched no key, which no check in this repo could have detected. scripts/check-opencode-permission-keys.sh now fails if OPENCODE_TOOLS and the schema diverge; its key list is pinned and dated rather than fetched, so CI cannot degrade to a silent pass on a network error, and --refresh compares the pin against the live schema on demand. Verified by reintroducing `write` and confirming the check exits 1. Still unset on every agent, and recorded as such rather than fixed blind: doom_loop, external_directory, lsp, question, todowrite - external_directory being the key #182 item 9 identifies as encoding this repo's worktree invariant, whose default deserves a deliberate decision rather than a sweep. NOT exercised against a live OpenCode binary in this pass - the generator, its drift check and the generated files are verified locally (26/26 parse as YAML; the drift check was confirmed to FAIL on a hand-edited command and on a stale command whose skill was deleted, not only to pass when in sync), but no live `opencode` run confirmed the commands appear in the TUI, so validated_against is unchanged. live run on 2026-09-23 against @opencode/cli 2.0.14 (`opencode2`), installed alongside the v1 binary which the package provides for exactly that. NOT CONFIRMED: per-skill discovery. v2 REMOVED the `debug skill` subcommand the v1 validation relied on — v2's debug surface is only `agents`, `config` and `paths` — so there is no CLI equivalent to enumerate discovered skills, and the /skill API route requires a running server. Skill discovery on v2 is therefore unverified, and docs/user/install/opencode.md's verification section was corrected because it instructed users to run two commands that no longer exist (`debug skill`, and `debug agent <name>` which is now `debug agents`, plural and without a per-agent argument). 2.0.15 review (2026-09-23, changelog-only, no live run): the 2.x line publishes NO GitHub release notes - `gh release list --repo anomalyco/opencode` still tops out at v1.18.32 - so the review was done off the tag range instead: v2.0.14...v2.0.15 is 42 commits across 250 files, which is NOT a trivial patch and was not treated as one. Nothing in the range touches agent definitions, skills, custom commands or MCP server config; the two near-misses are #50754 (install git plugins from branch subdirectories) and #50767 (log MCP OAuth/credential failures), both behaviour this repo does not depend on. reviewed_through advances to 2.0.15; validated_against stays at 2.0.14, the last version actually exercised live.

capability_source_note: targets.<key>.capabilities and capability_gaps are DERIVED from the capability registry and must not be hand-edited. Regenerate with `bash scripts/check-platform-targets.sh . --sync-capabilities`; `scripts/check-feature-equivalence.sh` fails when they drift.
version_claims_note: `validated_against` is the version this repo was last exercised against on a live maintainer machine. `reviewed_through` is the newest upstream release whose notes have actually been read for adapter impact. They are different claims and they drift apart on purpose: reading release notes is cheap and should always be current, while a live run needs a maintainer at a machine. V1-04 fires on `reviewed_through < latest_known` -- nobody has looked at what shipped -- because that is the gap a contributor can actually close. It deliberately does not fire on a validated_against lag, which is bounded instead by `last_reviewed` and V1-05's 90-day budget. A target with no `reviewed_through` falls back to `validated_against`, so consumer repos that have not adopted the field score exactly as before.
